world.rationale: AI drives the result: if superintelligence arrives I put AI-takeover doom near 4.5%, well above the card's 1%, because a takeover that disempowers most people is more likely to be permanent than recoverable, so I move weight from level 4 to level 5; that gives about 6% doom with superintelligence, about 1% without, and roughly 5% overall. I keep the other cards as floors and add knock-on channels, mainly for war (AI-sped arms races, bioweapons) and civil breakdown (job displacement and power concentration under superintelligence). I go below the energy card's 3.8% level-4 figure under superintelligence because I count AI systems seizing resources as AI takeover and expect faster substitution, and slightly below the civil-war card without superintelligence because breakdowns started by drought or shortages belong to climate or resources. Abundance for 90% of humanity is near zero without superintelligence and about 6% with it, capped by how fast Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia could be built out and whether the gains are shared.

places.rationale: Rich, stable, well governed and nearly energy self-sufficient, so modest growth is the default; without superintelligence slow growth and aging make stagnation the main alternative, and abundance needs the gains of superintelligence shared widely.

Strong institutions but 62% of energy imported, low fertility and slow growth leave real room for stagnation; with superintelligence it likely shares in the gains, though perhaps behind the US and China where the systems are built.
A quarter-century of flat incomes, very low fertility, high debt, 76% energy imports and growing heat and water stress make stagnation or decline more likely here than elsewhere in Europe.

Catch-up growth and energy exports favour improvement, but the Russia-Ukraine war, 10% of GDP on the military and weak governance make it the European region most exposed to war-driven decline or collapse.

The richest starting point, an energy exporter and home of frontier AI, so it gains most if superintelligence goes well; high inequality, polarisation, debt and its central place in the AI and nuclear rivalries keep a real tail of decline or collapse.
A low bar for a quarter's gain and abundant energy and minerals favour improvement, while the middle-income trap, high violence and heavy interest burdens keep stagnation and decline plausible.

Extreme water stress, rising heat, fragile politics and oil revenues that shrink as the world decarbonises make this one of the most collapse-prone regions, though cheap solar and desalination could carry it forward.

From a very low base a quarter's gain is likely, but the highest climate vulnerability, fragile states and fast population growth give it the largest collapse risk; abundance would need a build-out of unprecedented speed.
India's fast growth makes improvement the strong default, while humid heat, very high water stress, harvests and India-Pakistan nuclear risk drive the collapse tail.
Strong state capacity, manufacturing and AI capability favour gains, while the world's lowest fertility, fast aging and a possible war over Taiwan are the main downside risks.
Steady catch-up growth and a manufacturing role make improvement likely; sea-level rise, heat and storms on dense coasts and deltas, plus South China Sea tensions, make up the downside.
Dominated by rich, stable Australia and New Zealand with large energy and mineral exports, so improvement is likely; heat, drought and remoteness from conflict cut both ways.
